goldens.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dynamic import() calls in packages/app-store/index.ts fire at module-evaluation time, so the async import provides no lazy loading and all 27 app packages still load at startup

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/index.ts the appStore object is initialized with values like `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`. Because these `import()` expressions are executed during module evaluation (object literal creation), they will kick off loading immediately when `app-store/index.ts` is imported, rather than deferring until a specific integration is needed. This undermines the intended lazy-loading/perf benefit, even though behavior may still be functionally correct.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Changing appStore values to Promises breaks every appStore[key] consumer not updated in the diff, causing compile errors or silent 'not implemented' runtime regressions

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `appStore` entries from imported modules to `import()` Promises, and it updates many shown consumers to `await appStore[...]` (e.g., `getCalendar`, `videoClient`, payment handlers). The finding claims there are other `appStore[key]` consumers “not updated in the diff” that will break, but that cannot be verified from the provided diff alone. Within the shown changes, the updated call sites generally await the Promise, so the asserted widespread compile/runtime regressions are not demonstrated here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getCalendarCredentials in CalendarManager.ts returns items with a pending-Promise calendar field, so other callers get Promise<Calendar|null> where Calendar | null was promised and may call .deleteEvent on a Promise

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts`, `getCalendarCredentials` still does `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` but `getCalendar` was changed to `async` returning `Promise<Calendar | null>`. That means `getCalendarCredentials` now returns items whose `calendar` field is a pending Promise, not a `Calendar | null`. The diff shows at least one downstream fix (`getConnectedCalendars` now does `const calendar = await item.calendar;`), implying the contract changed and any other consumer not updated could try to call calendar methods (e.g., `.deleteEvent`) on a Promise at runtime or face a type mismatch.

reschedule.ts:125 (and wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125, viewer/bookings.tsx:553): forEach(async ...) destroys surrounding try/catch error handling, making the catch block dead code and causing unhandled promise rejections that can crash the server worker

handleCancelBooking.ts:462: credentials.forEach(async ...) has unawaited async callback, causing unhandled rejections from updateEvent and letting the handler finish before recurring-event calendar updates complete

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking.ts` the diff shows `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... })`. Using `forEach` with an `async` callback does not await the inner promises, so the handler can complete before the recurring-event calendar updates finish, and any rejection from `updateEvent`/other awaited calls inside that callback would not be propagated to the outer flow. This issue is directly introduced/exposed by making `getCalendar` async and then switching to `forEach(async ...)` without awaiting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarManager.ts:26-30: getCalendarCredentials still calls getCalendar synchronously so returned calendar field is a Promise, and other non-diff consumers of this exported API now hold Promises that are always truthy, bypassing null guards and causing runtime failures

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/CalendarManager.ts, getCalendarCredentials still does `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` without `await` (and the function itself isn’t `async`). Since getCalendar was changed to `async` and now returns `Promise<Calendar | null>`, the `calendar` field produced by getCalendarCredentials is indeed a Promise. The diff also shows one consumer adjusted for this (`getConnectedCalendars` now does `const calendar = await item.calendar;`), but the claim about “other non-diff consumers” and resulting runtime failures can’t be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: reschedule.ts:125 forEach(async) conversion neither serializes nor parallelizes — worse than either await Promise.all(map) or synchronous loop

adjudication.rationale: In multiple places the diff changes `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => { ... })` to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` (e.g., `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts` and `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts`, also `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`). `Array.forEach` does not await async callbacks, so the surrounding `try { ... }` will not catch rejected promises from inside the callback, and the outer function will proceed/finish without waiting for deletes/updates to complete. This is a verifiable behavior change introduced by the diff and can break reschedule/cancel flows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test files exist in the diff despite changing public contracts of getCalendar (sync→async) and appStore (module→Promise) across seven packages, with no tests covering the Promise-treating-app-as-not-implemented path or the unhandled rejection path

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes public contracts and control flow in a nontrivial way (e.g., `getCalendar` becomes `async` and now `await`s `appStore[...]` in `packages/app-store/_utils/getCalendar.ts`, while `appStore` entries become `import(...)` Promises in `packages/app-store/index.ts`). The diff shows many call sites updated to `await getCalendar(...)`, but it includes no test additions/updates. Given the new Promise-based loading, there are new/changed behaviors that would benefit from coverage, such as the “not implemented” branch when a dynamically imported module doesn’t expose `lib.CalendarService`/`VideoApiAdapter`/`PaymentService`, and the lack of explicit handling if the dynamic `import(...)` rejects (e.g., `await appStore[...]` in `getCalendar`/`videoClient`/payment handlers has no try/catch). This is a concrete, diff-grounded testing gap rather than a generic ‘add more tests’ request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dynamic imports in packages/app-store/index.ts are invoked unconditionally at module-init time, so no laziness is achieved and the async migration delivers no benefit

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, the appStore object literal assigns values like `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`. Because these `import()` calls are evaluated while constructing the object at module initialization, they will start loading immediately rather than lazily on first access. So this change does not achieve deferred loading; it just turns each entry into an already-in-flight Promise, reducing/negating the intended benefit of the async migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: forEach(async ...) in reschedule.ts:125 (vital and wipemycalother libs) makes the surrounding try/catch dead code, causing unhandled rejections and silent reschedule failures

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`, the diff changes `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => { ... })` to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })`. `Array.forEach` does not await async callbacks, so any promises returned by `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` are not awaited and any errors thrown/rejected inside the async callback will not be caught by an outer synchronous `try/catch` (if present). adjudication_records.issue_text: getCalendarCredentials in CalendarManager.ts stores Promise<Calendar | null> in the calendar field with no type/naming change, creating an unawaited-Promise trap where truthiness checks always pass

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `getCalendar` async (returns `Promise<Calendar | null>`), but `getCalendarCredentials` in `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts` still does `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` and stores it in the returned object as `calendar` without awaiting or renaming. This means the `calendar` field is now a Promise, and any consumer that does a simple truthiness check on `item.calendar` (without `await`) would always see it as truthy, creating a realistic unawaited-Promise trap. In this diff, `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to `const calendar = await item.calendar;`, so it avoids the issue there, but the stored shape is still misleading and error-prone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-store/index.ts:4-31 — 'lazy' imports are actually invoked at module-evaluation time when the object literal is constructed, so all 28 app packages are still fetched eagerly on first import; values should be thunks or an accessor to achieve lazy loading

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/index.ts the object literal assigns each key to the result of `import("./...")`. Those `import()` expressions run immediately when the module is evaluated, so creating `appStore` triggers all dynamic imports up front (returning Promises), rather than deferring loading until a specific app is needed. Achieving true lazy loading would require storing thunks/accessors (e.g., `() => import(...)`) or similar, not executing `import()` during module initialization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: videoClient.ts:23-41 getVideoAdapters converted to a sequential for loop with per-credential await, serializing module resolution and adding cumulative latency on the getBusyVideoTimes path; same issue in handleCancelBooking.ts:477-481

adjudication.rationale: While appStore entries were changed from imported namespaces to dynamic `import()` Promises (packages/app-store/index.ts), the diff also updates `getCalendar` to be `async` and to `await appStore[...]` before doing feature detection (`"lib" in calendarApp`). In CalendarManager.ts the referenced line still calls `getCalendar(credential)` without `await`, but the diff shows consumers were adapted to treat it as a Promise: `getConnectedCalendars` now does `const calendar = await item.calendar;`. adjudication_records.issue_text: Async forEach inside try/catch in reschedule.ts:125 (vital and wipemycalother apps) makes the catch dead code; rejections become unhandled promise rejections instead of structured errors; should use Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))

adjudication.rationale: In both `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts` and `.../wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts`, the diff changes `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => { ... })` to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` inside a surrounding `try { ... } catch { ... }`. Because `Array.forEach` does not await async callbacks, any thrown error or rejected promise inside the async callback will not be caught by the outer `try/catch`, leading to unhandled rejections and making the `catch` ineffective for those failures. Using `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for...of` with `await` would make the error handling work as intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Converting forEach to serial for...of with await in handleCancelBooking.ts:474-486 changes calendar credential loading from parallel to sequential, adding latency for users with multiple calendars

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts the old code used `.forEach((credential) => { const calendar = getCalendar(credential); apiDeletes.push(calendar?.deleteEvent(...) as Promise); })`, which effectively queued all deleteEvent promises without awaiting between credentials (and `getCalendar` was synchronous then). After the change, `getCalendar` became async (it now awaits a dynamic import via `await appStore[...]`), and the code was rewritten to `for (const credential of calendarCredentials) { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); apiDeletes.push(calendar?.deleteEvent(...) as Promise); }`, which awaits each calendar module load sequentially. That can add latency for users with multiple calendar credentials compared to parallelizing the `getCalendar` calls with `Promise.all`.
